context:
Small PR. w1 is reading, not code. The runner passes platform, benchmark,
and scale into run_cell already (runner.py:145-154); threading scale to
the resolver is mechanical. For w4, the workflow step ordering makes a
$GITHUB_ENV timestamp trivial.
description:
The official/throughput cell path resolves its result JSON by
filename-glob + mtime instead of the stdout contract every other cell
uses (because `run-official` has no --quiet; documented at
tests/uat/throughput.py:13-16). The resolver has two real weaknesses,
verified on develop @ fc31f3604:

1. SUBSTRING PLATFORM MATCH (tests/uat/throughput.py:60-66): the glob
   `f"{benchmark_token}_*{platform_token}*.json"` with platform="duckdb"
   matches `tpch_sf1_pg_duckdb_sql_20260709.json`. The existing
   false-positive test (test_throughput.py:62-71) only checks
   postgresql (not a substring); the pg_duckdb->duckdb collision
   direction is untested. The glob also carries no scale token, so SF is
   entirely unfiltered.

2. ARBITRARY TIE-BREAK + WIDE CI WINDOW: max-mtime tie-break
   (throughput.py:70) is arbitrary within filesystem mtime granularity.
   Mitigated in production by sequential execution and per-cell
   started_after (captured before the subprocess launches,
   runner.py:157), but the nightly assert step widens the window to a
   full hour over a shared results dir
   (.github/workflows/nightly.yml:607-612) -- safe on a fresh CI runner,
   wrong-file-prone on any persistent runner or multi-cell sweep.

Context: #1119 (d48231a3b) fixed a genuine TEST-only mtime race
(_MTIME_SLACK backdating); production was mostly sound. This TODO fixes
the remaining production weaknesses.
